source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: An address change can be done entirely online, while the manual sends a name change to an MVD or authorized third party office with identification in both names.
corrections.note: Address-online part is on page six while name-change office part is on page seven.

corrections.corrected_statement: Each front seat occupant must wear a properly adjusted and fastened lap and shoulder belt while the vehicle is in motion, or where only a lap belt is installed the lap belt alone must be properly adjusted and fastened.
corrections.note: Added the exception that only the lap belt is required where that is all that is installed.

corrections.corrected_statement: The lap belt prevents ejection and protects the lower body, while the shoulder belt protects the head and chest from the dashboard and windshield.
corrections.note: Lap belt wording is on page nineteen with shoulder wording continuing on page twenty.

corrections.corrected_statement: If someone is tailgating you, slow down gradually and open more space ahead, so you can brake more gently and give the tailgater time to react.
corrections.note: The gradual slow down wording starts on page 25, not page 26.

corrections.corrected_statement: Passing on the right is allowed only when it is safe and the other driver is turning left or you are on an open highway or in a business or residential district where the road is marked for two or more lanes going the same way as you, and you must never go off the paved part of the road to pass on the right and must never pass on the left of a driver who has signaled a left turn.
corrections.note: Added the multi lane cases and the ban on leaving the pavement.

corrections.corrected_statement: A tailgater is handled by slowing gradually and adding space ahead of you, which lets you brake more gently when you must stop.
corrections.note: The gradual slow down wording starts on page 25, not page 26.

corrections.corrected_statement: Know where you want to go as you approach a roundabout, follow the signs and get in the appropriate lane.
corrections.note: Changed right lane to appropriate lane as the page states.

corrections.corrected_statement: If you run a red light and cause a crash that results in life-threatening injuries to another driver or passenger, you may be fined up to five hundred dollars and your driving privilege may be suspended for three months and you may be ordered to perform community service.
corrections.note: Corrected fine from 00 to five hundred dollars as stated on the page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Wrong-way driving appears both as a 2-point violation and, on a controlled-access highway, as a ground for MVD action.
corrections.note: The controlled-access-highway clause appears on page 64, not page 63.

corrections.corrected_statement: If you believe an officer acted inappropriately, contact the officer's agency and ask to speak to a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop.
corrections.note: The full statement starts on page 73 and continues onto page 74.

corrections.corrected_statement: When a crash involves no serious physical injury or death, vehicles must be removed from the main traveled portion of the roadway if they remain safely operable under their own power without needing towing and moving them does not cause further damage or increase traffic hazards.
corrections.note: Added the missing condition about no further damage or increased hazards.

corrections.corrected_statement: A complaint about an officer's conduct goes to the officer's agency, where you can ask for a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop.
corrections.note: The full statement starts on page 73 and continues onto page 74.

corrections.corrected_statement: While driving you may use a wireless device only to report an emergency or for hands-free or voice to text operation.
corrections.note: Added the hands-free and voice-to-text exception the page also allows.

corrections.corrected_statement: Foresight is about sizing up a situation fast and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and right action.
corrections.note: The awareness and planning wording is on page twenty-two, not page twenty-three.

corrections.corrected_statement: While driving you may use a wireless device only to report an emergency or for hands-free or voice to text operation, and otherwise you must pull off the road safely and stop to use a cell phone or send or receive a text message.
corrections.note: Added the hands-free and voice-to-text exception the page also allows.

corrections.corrected_statement: Children should not fly kites or model airplanes near the overhead power lines used by light rail.
corrections.note: The kids-specific warning starts on page 49 and continues onto page 50.

corrections.corrected_statement: Most crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car turns in front of a motorcycle, usually because the driver did not see it or misjudged its distance and speed.
corrections.note: The sentence begins on page 50, not page 51.
